screening_decisions.reason: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial of DDAVP in elective aortic surgery. Compares DDAVP to placebo, assesses blood loss and transfusion requirements. Meets all criteria: RCT, DDAVP vs placebo, perioperative, adult surgical patients without inherited bleeding disorders.
Double-blind randomized prospective trial of DDAVP vs placebo in hip replacement. Measures total blood loss. Fulfills RCT design, appropriate comparator, surgical population, and outcomes.
Study design is a meta-analysis, not a randomised controlled trial. The review includes only RCTs. Therefore not eligible.

RCT with four arms including DDAVP, aprotinin (active comparator), and no treatment. Compares DDAVP to aprotinin and to no treatment. Performed during CPB surgery, adults without inherited bleeding disorders. Relevant design and comparator per inclusion criteria.

Prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of DDAVP in CABG patients on aspirin. Meets all criteria: RCT, DDAVP vs placebo, perioperative, adult surgical patients with acquired platelet inhibition (not inherited bleeding disorder).

Though patients were randomized, the control group received no DDAVP and no placebo infusion (no sham). The protocol requires comparison to placebo or an active comparator; a 'no treatment' arm without blinding is not a valid control under this inclusion criterion. Additionally, absence of blinding may introduce bias. Therefore excluded.

Prospective, double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT. DDAVP vs placebo in cardiac surgery patients identified by a point-of-care test as having platelet dysfunction (acquired). Assesses blood loss and transfusion. Meets all criteria.

This is an RCT of DDAVP vs saline after hydroxyethyl starch infusion, but it only reports laboratory coagulation parameters (von Willebrand factor activity) and does not assess perioperative blood loss or transfusion needs. The objective of the review is efficacy in reducing blood loss/transfusion, so this study does not contribute relevant outcome data. Excluded as not measuring key clinical outcomes.
Not a clinical trial; it is a summary of guideline recommendations. Study design does not meet inclusion criteria (RCT).

Double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT of DDAVP in total hip replacement. Compares DDAVP to placebo, measures blood loss and transfusion. Eligible: RCT design, appropriate comparator, surgical population.
Double-blind, placebo-controlled randomised trial. DDAVP vs placebo in patients with excessive bleeding after CPB. Assesses blood loss and transfusion. Meets all inclusion criteria.

RCT (saline control group). DDAVP given intraoperatively during rewarming, placebo (equal volume saline) in control. Assesses blood loss and transfusion. Eligible: RCT, DDAVP vs placebo, cardiac surgery patients, no inherited bleeding disorder.

Randomised controlled trial comparing intranasal DDAVP to blood transfusion (active treatment) in cirrhotic patients undergoing dental extraction. Cirrhosis-associated coagulopathy is acquired, not inherited. Comparator is not a hemostatic pharmacological agent but is an active intervention. Given the review's focus on perioperative DDAVP efficacy, this trial provides relevant data. Included conservatively.
Double-blind randomized trial of DDAVP vs placebo in primary total hip/knee arthroplasty. Measures postoperative bleeding and transfusion. Fulfills all criteria.

Described as a study of 12 patients where six received desmopressin; no mention of randomization or blinding. It is not a randomised controlled trial, so does not meet the inclusion criteria for study design.
Randomized clinical trial; patients randomly allocated to DDAVP or saline placebo before sinus surgery. Assesses blood loss. Meets criteria: RCT, DDAVP vs placebo, perioperative.
Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial of DDAVP in spinal fusion. Assesses operative blood loss and transfusion. Eligible design and comparator.
Double-blind randomized trial comparing DDAVP to saline placebo in myocardial revascularization patients with recent aspirin use. Measures transfusion requirements. Meets all criteria.
Double-blind placebo-controlled RCT with three arms: aprotinin, DDAVP, and placebo. DDAVP compared to both placebo and active comparator (aprotinin). Assesses blood loss and transfusion. Eligible.

Randomized double-blind study of DDAVP vs saline placebo after CABG. Although primary focus was hemodynamics, postoperative blood loss was measured. The study is an RCT with relevant outcomes, so included.
Double-blind, randomised, prospective trial of DDAVP vs placebo in CPB patients. Assesses total blood loss and transfusion. Eligible.
Double-blind study with random assignment to DDAVP or placebo. Evaluates operative blood loss in neuromuscular scoliosis surgery. Meets criteria.
Randomized double-blind trial of DDAVP vs placebo in routine CABG. Measures postoperative blood loss and transfusion. Eligible.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis, not an RCT. Does not evaluate DDAVP. Excluded because it does not meet the study design or intervention requirements.
Methodological article on statistical testing for funnel plot asymmetry in meta-analyses. Not an RCT and does not examine DDAVP. Excluded.

Prospective, blinded, randomized trial comparing repeated doses of DDAVP vs placebo in CABG surgery. Outcomes include blood loss and blood product replacement. No inherited bleeding disorders mentioned.
Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of DDAVP in primary CABG. Assesses blood loss, hemoglobin loss, and transfusion requirements.
Double-blind, randomized study of DDAVP vs placebo in cardiac operations. Evaluates bleeding by blood loss and replacement volume.
This is a letter to the editor commenting on morphine use in children, not a trial. Does not involve DDAVP as an intervention and does not study blood loss/transfusion outcomes.
Randomized, blinded comparison of DDAVP vs placebo in children undergoing cardiac surgery. Evaluates blood loss and blood replacement. No inherited bleeding disorders.
Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled parallel group trial of DDAVP in uncomplicated CABG. Assesses bleeding time and postoperative blood loss.
Retrospective cohort study of patients who decline transfusion; does not evaluate DDAVP intervention. Not an RCT.

Randomized trial evaluating DDAVP for prevention of catheter-induced thrombosis, not for reducing perioperative blood loss or transfusion. Outcome is thrombosis, not blood loss, which does not match review objective.

Double-blind RCT of DDAVP vs placebo before percutaneous kidney biopsy. Evaluates incidence of bleeding complications and hematoma size. Biopsy is an invasive procedure included in the criteria. No inherited bleeding disorders.
Clinical practice guideline on von Willebrand disease diagnosis and management. Not a randomized trial, not evaluating DDAVP for perioperative blood loss.
Double-blind, randomized clinical trial of DDAVP vs placebo in scoliosis surgery. Evaluates blood loss and coagulation factors. No inherited bleeding disorders.

Double-blind RCT comparing two doses of DDAVP vs placebo in total hip arthroplasty for rheumatoid arthritis. Evaluates total blood loss and red cell transfusion requirements. No inherited bleeding disorders.

Study investigates DDAVP to reduce blood transfusion requirements in cardiac surgery patients with aspirin-induced platelet dysfunction. Aspirin-induced dysfunction is acquired, not inherited. Although abstract is truncated and RCT design not fully confirmed, title and objective suggest a controlled study; being conservative and including.
Review article summarizing DDAVP use in hematological disorders and surgical bleeding prevention. Not a primary trial, not an RCT.
This is a brief report summary (likely a commentary or journal highlight) of the kidney biopsy trial (Study 34). It is not a separate primary randomized trial.
Review article on transfusion reactions; does not evaluate DDAVP as an intervention. Not an RCT.
Placebo-controlled, randomized clinical trial of preoperative DDAVP in burn débridement and grafting surgery. Evaluates blood loss per percent body surface area. No inherited bleeding disorders.
Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of DDAVP in elective cardiac surgery with CPB. Assesses postoperative blood loss and blood product replacement.
National survey of RBC utilization patterns; does not evaluate DDAVP. Not an RCT.
Observational study of reoperation for bleeding after CABG; does not study DDAVP intervention. Not an RCT.
Clinical guideline on platelet transfusions; does not evaluate DDAVP. Not a randomized trial.

Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of DDAVP in cardiac surgery patients with active bleeding despite tranexamic acid pretreatment. Evaluates RBC transfusion requirements and blood loss. DDAVP vs placebo comparison.
Methodological paper on detecting bias in meta-analyses using funnel plots. Not a clinical trial; does not involve DDAVP.
Review article on cellular mechanisms of DDAVP hemostatic effects. Not a clinical trial, not an RCT evaluating perioperative outcomes.

Randomized, prospective, double-blind clinical trial of DDAVP vs placebo in spinal cord injury patients undergoing flap reconstruction of pelvic pressure sores. Evaluates intraoperative blood loss and transfusion requirements. No inherited bleeding disorders.

Randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial comparing DDAVP to placebo in adult patients undergoing elective CABG. Assesses perioperative blood loss and transfusion. No inherited bleeding disorders. Meets all selection criteria.
Study population is a patient with Bernard-Soulier syndrome, an inherited bleeding disorder. The review excludes people with inherited bleeding disorders.
This is a clinical practice guideline, not a randomised controlled trial. Study design does not meet inclusion criteria.
Not a randomised trial: patients who received desmopressin were selected based on increased bleeding tendency, and the other groups were defined by prior antiplatelet therapy, not randomisation.
This is a clinical practice guideline update, not a randomised controlled trial of DDAVP.
This is a meta-analysis of existing trials, not a primary randomised controlled trial. Inclusion criteria specify randomised controlled trials.
Meta-analysis of multiple trials, not a single randomised controlled trial. Does not meet the requirement for a primary RCT.
This is a narrative review discussing alternatives to platelet transfusion, not a randomised controlled trial of DDAVP.
Described as a prospective single-blind study, but no mention of random assignment. Not clearly an RCT; therefore does not meet the strict inclusion criteria for randomised controlled trials.
Single-arm study (all patients received desmopressin) with no concurrent control group. Not a randomised controlled trial.

Although randomised, the study was conducted in uremic patients about to commence haemodialysis, not in the context of surgery or an invasive procedure; outcomes were purely laboratory measures of platelet function. Does not meet the requirement that DDAVP/TXA be given before, during or immediately after surgery/invasive procedures with clinical bleeding/transfusion outcomes.
Non-randomised before-and-after study comparing two consecutive cohorts; not a randomised controlled trial.
Prospective, randomised, double-blind trial comparing DDAVP to placebo in children undergoing cardiac surgery. Assesses postoperative blood loss. No inherited bleeding disorder.
Randomised, placebo-controlled trial comparing DDAVP, tranexamic acid, and saline in patients undergoing total knee replacement. Compares DDAVP to both placebo and an active comparator.
Double-blind, placebo-controlled randomised trial comparing DDAVP to placebo in adult cardiac surgical patients. Assesses perioperative blood loss and transfusion.
Pharmacokinetic/healthy volunteer study; not a randomised controlled trial in a surgical population nor does it report perioperative bleeding/transfusion outcomes.
Randomised, controlled, double-blind trial comparing DDAVP to saline in patients undergoing elective partial hepatectomy. Assesses intraoperative blood loss and transfusion.
Duplicate record of study 62. Non-randomised before-and-after study; not an RCT.

Double-blind randomised trial with four arms: placebo, tranexamic acid only, desmopressin only, and both. Compares DDAVP to placebo and to an active comparator in cardiac surgery patients. Reports blood loss and transfusion.
Double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial of DDAVP in patients undergoing complex cardiac surgery requiring CPB. Assesses operative and postoperative blood loss.
Randomised trial comparing DDAVP to placebo in adult patients undergoing cardiopulmonary bypass during cardiac surgery. Reports postoperative bleeding time, blood loss, and transfusion requirements.
Randomised, double-blind trial comparing DDAVP to placebo in patients undergoing primary elective CABG. Examines perioperative blood loss and coagulation, though primary focus is hemodynamics.

Prospective randomised trial: two groups (DDAVP alone vs DDAVP plus tranexamic acid). Effectively compares DDAVP with and without an active comparator (tranexamic acid) in CABG patients, addressing perioperative blood loss.
Systematic review and meta-analysis focused on tranexamic acid, not a primary RCT of DDAVP. Does not meet inclusion criteria for either study design or intervention.
Consensus/narrative review of antiplatelet testing, not a randomised controlled trial and does not directly study DDAVP. Excluded based on study design and population/intervention.
This is a narrative review, not a randomized controlled trial. It does not present original data from an RCT.

This is a prospective, placebo-controlled, double-blinded clinical trial in which patients were randomly divided into desmopressin and placebo groups. Participants are adults undergoing CABG without inherited bleeding disorders (although on anti-platelet medication, acquired). The intervention is DDAVP, and outcomes include blood loss and transfusion requirements. Meets all selection criteria.

The abstract describes a comparison with a control group, but no mention of random allocation. It does not clearly state that it was a randomized trial, and thus it is unlikely to qualify as an RCT. It may be a non-randomized or retrospective comparison.
This is a methodological paper about Cochrane review standards, completely unrelated to desmopressin or surgical bleeding. It is not an RCT.
This is a systematic review on liver biopsy techniques; it does not involve desmopressin, surgical blood loss, or transfusion. It is not an RCT.
This is a case series reporting adverse events in four children. It is not a randomized trial, and no comparison group or systematic assessment of efficacy is provided.

This is a prospective, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial of desmopressin in patients undergoing valvular heart surgery, reporting blood loss and transfusion outcomes. Meets all criteria.
This is a meta-analysis of randomized trials, not itself an original RCT. The review requires individual RCTs.

This is a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of desmopressin given perioperatively to patients undergoing aortic valve replacement. Participants have acquired platelet dysfunction, not inherited bleeding disorders. Primary and secondary outcomes include blood loss and transfusion-related endpoints. Meets all selection criteria.

This double-blind, placebo-controlled study investigates desmopressin in patients undergoing aorto-iliac graft surgery. While the abstract does not explicitly state 'randomized', the design (double-blind, placebo-controlled) is typical of an RCT and likely to be randomized. Outcomes include blood loss and transfusion. Given the conservative approach, it is included.

This is a prospective, double-blind RCT in which healthy young patients undergoing spinal fusion were randomly allocated to desmopressin or placebo. Blood loss was a primary outcome. Meets all criteria.

This is a prospective, randomized, double-blind trial comparing desmopressin with placebo in patients undergoing complex congenital heart operations. Participants have congenital heart disease but no inherited bleeding disorder. Outcomes include blood loss and transfusion. Meets all selection criteria.

This article focuses on von Willebrand's disease, an inherited bleeding disorder. The review specifically excludes patients with inherited bleeding disorders. Not an RCT of surgery without inherited disorders.
This is a clinical practice guideline, not an original research study. It does not report an RCT.
This is a prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of desmopressin in CABG patients. Outcomes include mediastinal chest tube drainage and blood product use. Meets all criteria.
This is a single-arm, dose-escalation phase II trial without a randomized comparator group. It does not meet the review's requirement for an RCT with a control group (placebo or active comparator).

This study randomized 66 patients undergoing elective CABG into desmopressin and control groups and evaluated blood loss and transfusion. It is an RCT, participants have no inherited bleeding disorder. Meets criteria.
This is a meta-analysis of RCTs, not an original RCT. The review requires individual RCTs.
This is a double-blind, randomized, prospective trial in 100 patients on CPB, comparing desmopressin to placebo. Blood loss and transfusion outcomes were assessed. Meets all criteria.

This is a prospective, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial specifically in CABG patients on aspirin preoperatively. Desmopressin was compared to placebo, and postoperative blood loss and transfusion were outcomes. Meets all criteria.

The study divided 200 consecutive patients into control and treatment groups without random allocation; the first 100 patients received no medication and the next 100 received DDAVP. This is not a randomized trial, and the outcome is ecchymosis/hematoma, not quantified perioperative blood loss or red cell transfusion. Does not meet RCT criteria nor the required outcomes.

This is a randomized, double-blind, prospective study comparing desmopressin with placebo in patients undergoing total hip replacement. Outcomes include bleeding time, coagulation factors, and indirectly blood loss. Meets RCT criteria, participants have no inherited bleeding disorder.
This is a prospective randomized trial in 62 CABG patients, comparing intraoperative desmopressin to placebo. Outcomes include total blood loss and red cell transfusions. Meets all criteria.

This is a randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial of desmopressin in children with cerebral palsy undergoing spinal fusion. Estimated blood loss and transfusion were outcomes. No inherited bleeding disorders. Meets all criteria.
This is a meta-analysis, not an original RCT. It does not meet the study design criterion.
